4.Voiding cystourethrogram (VCUG) - Criterion standard for diagnosis of vesicoureteral reflux
• ultrasound, CT and VCUG (voiding cystourethrogram). to\nconfirm urachal abnormalities.

○ Voiding Cystourethrogram (VCUG); some recommend it ​before discharge of patients from hospital,\nwhereas others prefer delay for 2-6 wk ​(to allow inflammation in the bladder to resolve to reduce the\nincidence of vesicoureteral reflux).

The “bottom-up” method was a renal sonogram plus a voiding cystourethrogram (VCUG), which will identify upper and lower urinary tract abnormalities, including VUR, bladder–bowel dysfunction, andbladder abnormalities, such as a paraureteral diverticulum.

qs.q: An 8-month-old infant with a documented second febrile urinary tract infection has completed antibiotic treatment and sterile urine cultures are confirmed. When is the classic time to perform a voiding cystourethrogram?
o: Four to six weeks after the infection
qs.e: Classic teaching recommends performing voiding cystourethrogram 4 to 6 weeks after the acute infection has cleared to avoid false positives from transient inflammation. Immediate testing during acute infection is not recommended due to altered bladder dynamics.

qs.q: A voiding cystourethrogram (VCUG) is performed on a 2-year-old girl with pyelonephritis, demonstrating contrast reflux into the ureter and renal pelvis with mild dilation and well-preserved caliceal fornices. Which grade of vesicoureteral reflux does this represent?
qs.e: Grade III VUR is defined by mild dilation of the renal pelvis and ureter without the loss of calyces. Grade II shows no dilation, Grade IV has moderate dilation with loss of calyces, and Grade V shows severe dilation with tortuosity.

qs.q: A voiding cystourethrogram is performed on a 3-year-old boy to investigate recurrent urinary tract infections, revealing contrast reflux into the renal pelvis with mild calyceal blunting. How is this grade of vesicoureteral reflux classified?
o: Severe tortuosity and massive dilation of the entire collecting system
Contrast confined strictly to the distal ureter without reaching the pelvis
Reflux into the collecting system with complete effacement of all calyces
Mild dilation of the renal pelvis and ureter without loss of calyces
qs.e: Grade III VUR represents mild dilation of the renal pelvis and ureter without loss of calyces. Grade V features severe dilation and a tortuous ureter.

qs.q: A 4-year-old girl with a history of recurrent febrile urinary tract infections undergoes an abdominal ultrasound that reveals moderate upper tract dilation. Which finding provides the definitive indication for proceeding with a voiding cystourethrogram?
qs.e: A voiding cystourethrogram is indicated to evaluate for vesicoureteral reflux when renal ultrasound shows unexplained hydronephrosis. Heavy proteinuria or elevated serum creatinine reflects glomerular or advanced parenchymal disease rather than structural reflux indications.
